title: 5 lifting conspiracy theories
summary: NH shares five unproven hunches about lifting. Strapped holds may grow the forearms as well as or better than bare-hand grip. Protein (and calorie) needs are vastly overstated by an industry born from 70s magazines selling whey. Exercise changes how cholesterol and sugar affect you. Sleep apnea and chub rub come from fat, not neck or leg muscle. And the pump and mind-muscle connection are myths compared with fiber damage from progressive overload.
claims: 'Conspiracy theory' is a dishonest label for ideas science or media haven't ruled on yet; his theories are just unproven hunches
Straps only stop the bar rolling; you're still holding it, so strapped holds with heavier loads may stretch and grow the forearms at least as well as bare-hand grip
Grip strength and forearm size are separate qualities, like strength and size
Protein needs are vastly overrated: he eats 50-60 g a day sometimes and still grows and gains strength
The lowest protein values in studies still aren't the true minimum
High-protein dogma was manufactured by 70s bodybuilding magazines to create a market for whey protein
Someone weighing about 180 lb who eats 200 g of protein a day is wasting money
Calorie needs are also overrated; fitness YouTubers lie about intake just as they inflate height and body fat (often off by 5%)
He maintains his mass on about 2000 kcal a day
Eating stacks of eggs to look like Arnold and avoiding all cholesterol are both extremes
Physical activity probably changes how dietary cholesterol affects you: harmful when sedentary, possibly beneficial for testosterone when active
Insulin sensitivity depends on exercise; sugar after training affects you differently than after sitting on the couch. You can 'out-health' a bad diet
Studies linking neck growth to sleep apnea involve men who also got fat all over; muscular neck growth shouldn't cause apnea
He had sleep apnea at 240 lb with the same neck size he has now, and none since dropping the fat
Chub rub comes from fat, not muscle: with 26-27 in thighs he has none, but he had it at 240 lb
The pump is useless compared with muscle fiber damage from tension and progressive overload; pros grow from drugs, not pumps
He trains in arctic conditions 8 months a year, never gets a pump, and still grows
Not feeling the muscle doesn't stop it growing; he doesn't feel his legs when squatting, yet they grow like weeds
The mind-muscle connection is only useful for muscles you struggle to target, which is really a form issue
exercises: Strapped holds / heavy pulls with straps
his hypothesis: weighted stretch on forearms with more load than bare grip allows
